text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":0.75,"launches":1,"pipeline":2.5,"footprint":0.5},"rationale":"Five numerical-passing, compiling observations, all pinned at 32768 actual smem (hard portability cap). Best is attempt-02 (64x128x32, stages=2, swizzle=16) at 399.54 us; attempt-03 (same tile/config but stages=1) is 408.93 us, and attempt-01/04 (64x128x64, stages=1) are ~402.23 us. Simulated DRAM is flat at 16.78 MB in every run, so the analytical serpentine panel-reuse traffic term is NOT materializing as measured traffic; swizzle=0 vs 4 vs 8 vs 16 has produced indistinguishable latency at matched tile (attempt-01 vs attempt-04 both 402.23 us for 64x128x64 stages=1). Therefore down-weight traffic from 1 to 0.75 (analytic term unreliable, measured DRAM flat), raise pipeline from 2 to 2.5 as deeper staging at small block_K is the clearest observed lever (attempt-02 best). Keep footprint at 0.5 since the hard cap already enforces it, and launches at 1 to avoid overfitting five points. Keep full tile/stage/swizzle domains so HiGHS can trade smaller block_M for stages=3 under the 32KB cap and still test swizzle at matched tile/stage. Next hypothesis: since block_K=32 with stages=2 beat stages=1 at matched tile, probe block_M=32 (or 64x64x32) with stages=3 to test whether deeper pipelining lowers simulated latency further, and compare swizzle=0 vs 16 at that exact matched configuration; if swizzle still shows no latency or DRAM effect, narrow swizzle toward [0,4] in the next revision. Validation scope: Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed."}
